title: Your dreams on the next RPG Maker (RMMV updates or brand new ones)

posts.author: DoubleX
posts.body:
I know it's far too early to even imagine on this, as RMMV has just released for less than 1 month and RMMV will be constantly updated. But let's say RPG Maker MV Ace(or RMMV updates in any other form, or even brand new RM, same below) would come eventually, what would you want RPG Maker MV Ace to have?
I've briefly searched for this in all RMMV communities I know, and I think quite some of you would want some of these:
1. Javascript ES6(or later versions if they would exist at the time RPG Maker MV Ace would be decided to be made and they would be even better than ES6 for the would be RPG Maker MV Ace)
2. PIXI V3(or later versions if they would exist at the time RPG Maker MV Ace would be decided to be made and they would be even better than PIXI V3 for the would be RPG Maker MV Ace)
3. RMXP Mapping or even better ones
4. Plugin manager parameter readers being able to read the js file name and/or the one in the plugin manager(instead of PluginManager.parameters("Fixed File Name"))
5. Folders in the plugin manager to prevent plugin manager bloat and improve plugin organizations(like grouping them by authors, plugin types, etc)
6. Built-in js IDE rivaling existing ones for generic js development but specifically built for the would be RPG Maker MV Ace(having accesses to both the default RMMV codebase and custom plugins)
7. Built-in Android/IOS Emulators rivaling those for generic android/ios app development(but they would only need to run the game and nothing else)
8. Improved FPSMeter opening accesses to the frame rate(right now it's hardcoded as always 60)
9. Built in Version Control System for game projects(or even Distributed Version Control System if it were needed)
None of your wants here need to be realistic, as it's up to those would be developing RPG Maker MV Ace to decide if our wants would be feasible. After all, one can always dream right?

posts.author: arcthemonkey

I don't know, I honestly don't miss the resource manager even a little. I would like to see some very basic drawing functionality in the editor, though. Like, give me a pencil and a color step palette.
Actually, here is my #1 request for every RPG Maker in the future:
A map editor that lets me a ) break the grid (i.e pixel-based tile placement), and/or b ) use 24/24 tiles with a 48/48 design with the same base resolution as MV currently has. b ) alone would give you insanely more control over the appearance of your maps, and a ) would remove a lot of the need for parallax mapping. Maybe let us rotate tiles, too? kthxbye
Here's the rest of my wishlist:
1) Tilesets with unlimited height, or at least greatly expanded height. I mean seriously, give us triple what we have now and I'll be happy. I understand trying to keep it mobile friendly, but if I wanted to make a PC-only game with larger maps and tilesets, I should be able to.
2) Related to 1), maybe give us a mobile/PC setting for our projects. Mobile games would be limited similar to the current MV, while PC mode would remove a lot of those silly restrictions.
3) Please, please, PLEASE bring back the "Wall" attribute tag from older RPG Makers (The one that let you walk under walls in the up/down direction for only 1 tile).
4) A greatly expanded character generator. I'd like to see one that can be used to make villagers out of the box, including children, with more than 15 odd something clothes options. Maybe even a monster tab for humanoid monsters like werewolves, zombies, skeletons, etc. I think that the current generator is almost there, but it cripples itself unnecessarily by doing silly things like restricting options to specific genders, without providing anything of value in the process. Give use an "Adult" tab with a body section that let use pick male human, female human, skeleton, lycanthrope/cat person, whatever. On the clothes tab, give us some gender neutral options (we don't need male and female versions of plate male) and then a collection of armors and plain villager clothes in both gender styles
regardless of which body we picked
.
Seriously,  this is basically what it already does. I just want the training wheels taken off, please!
5) Built in, simple particle systems like Archeia mentioned above. I don't need anything procedural or fancy like that (I don't know that that would match up with the RPG Maker style well), but it would be cool to be able to have a simple emitter spitting out some small smoke sprites or something. In the editor, simple would be best:
Image:
Direction:
Speed:
Spread/Variance:
Size/Variance:
Lifespan:
Then if people wanted to do fancy crap they could use script it.
6) Old School auto-tile animation with variable frames. I missing being able to have a 16-frame water animation if I want to without having to fiddle around with scripts.
I mean, here are a ton of stuff they could do. I'd love to see built-in mode 7 support, and a third "Action" battle system option (Hey, they could combine this with the character generator and the particle system for projectiles!), but I'm trying to be realistic

- More than 4 Self-Switches in the GUI.  I know the back-end supports an arbitrary number, so at least having, say, 12 would be nice.  I assume this would be a trivial change to some constants in the Editor.
- Ability to use existing VX Ace resources such as Sprites and Tilesets without resizing.  I know plug-ins let you go to 32x32, but the editor still looks strange.

An event teleport can't work that way - and I really doubt that even Zelda worked that way.
That is because to teleport an event to another map, that map needs to run in memory - and that is difficult enough with single maps, much less every map in game.
The only thing possible is to pretend such a thing by vanishing an event from a map, storing how long it was gone, and have it appear at an approximate place in the new map after the player follows it. But never process the steps of an event done while the player is not on that map. That way lies hell...

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
amerk said:
but I've also heard parallax maps tend to really drive the size of a project up. Would an in-game parallax mapping do the same?
Click to expand...
Yes - in tileset mapping, every tile on a map is a single number (the number of the tile inside the tileset). You'll only need to store the 48x48 pixel colors of the tile once for as many maps as you want.
In parallax mapping, you need the color code for every pixel on every position of every map - that's 48x48 color codes per tile in the grid, or 2304 color codes for the tile that is stored in a single number in tileset mapping. Depending on how much bits your color code has and how many layers are on the tileset map the factor might be different, but with 3 layers (MV) and 24bit color (the usual color palette of parallax mapping, you don't parallax with 8Bit/256 colors) that is a size factor of more than 2000 times the memory for parallax maps as compared to tileset maps.

That's the way it works now ... sort of. You create a new Event that copies everything that's in the old Event. A reference wouldn't need it's own Event entry shown and wouldn't need to store any information except for a pointer. If you change the original or any reference, they all change.
Say for instance that you want to cover a 5 tile wide hallway with a single Event that happens when the player gets to that point. Typically, you'll create one Event and then copy and paste it four more times to cover the width of the hallway. If you want to change this Event, you either have to change it 5 times or delete 4 of them, change it and then copy and paste it back where you need it. Either way, you still have 5 Events when you only wanted one (and 5x the memory requirement). You also have 5 entries in your Events list getting in the way.

Click to expand...
Doesn't work that way - if you go beyond a certain number, you will need to restructure the data formats.
Example: you decide to allow for 255 different tiles per map, that will require you to reserve one byte for each map position (because one byte can store the numbers between 0 and 255.
If you decide to allow for 270 different tiles, then for each map position you'll need a way to store the numbers from 0 to 270 - which is not possible with one byte, you'll need two byte per map position. So allowing even one more tile than 255 different tiles on the map/tileset will double the memory needed for storing the map.
Of course you can then define a lot more than 270 different tiles (2 bytes can store numbers up to 65535), but the memory usage is doubled.
And if your regular maps usually need only 200 different tiles, then that is wasted space.
The maps of RM are stored a bit differently, they don't use exactly two bytes and they need to store the different layers differently, but the way the data of the map is stored needs to be fixed at the beginning (allowing different save structures would cause for additional performance problems).
Yes, there are plugins to change the way how the map data is stored - but then they need to handle that entirely differently, which means they have to obey their own limits and numbers. Providing different ways by default is not cost-effective - do you want to pay double the price for the program, just to give a minority of the users the option to switch to a different handling that has almost no effect on most users or games?

posts.author: Engr. Adiktuzmiko
posts.body:
@Piyan Glupak
RM supports cases... but you need to script call it XD
Spoiler
on Ace it is "case.. when"
case var
when value
when value
else //when all whens are false
//and so on
end
on MV it is Switch..case"
switch (expression) {
case 1;
case 2;
default; //when all cases are false
//and so on;
}
Cases are kinda hard to implement as an Event command because cases are normally used in long situations that make them look better than ifs, and highly dynamic in length. The same is probably the reason why the Conditional Branch Event command only has If-then-else and cannot do if-then-elseif...-else. This is if we're talking of the current way that event commands are "converted" into code in-game.
The only way I can see it being implemented with the current set-up will be if the case constructor/opener, the individual cases and the case closing are placed as individual event commands (meaning 3 different event command buttons), but it seems counter intuitive to me, and not very different to the current method on how you'd do it via combining Script calls and event commands that I will write below.
You can tell the engine to go into case mode and check each case via script call event command and run event commands as the actions for each cases using the normal event commands way.
For Ace
Spoiler
Script: case expression // initiates the case clause
when value1
Create Event Commands Here
Script: when value2
Create Event Commands Here
repeat as many times as needed
Script: end //closes the case clause
For MV
Spoiler
Script: switch (expression) {
//opens the switch clause
case 1;
Create Event Commands Here
Script: case 2;
Create Event Commands Here
repeat as many times as needed
Script: } //closes the switch clause
And poof you now have used cases in Events.
and ofc if you know RGSSx or JavaScript more, you can just go full Script call mode.

Yes, but there are reasons for this - licencing for MP3 for example means that only free converters can use the free licence, if you sell a program that contains an MP3 encoder (as opposed to a decoder for playing), then you (as the developer) are required to pay for the licence, and have to get that money back from your customers.

A lot of things have been said on other places on why unlimited tilesets and 3D are very bad ideas, so I only comment on MP3 and JPG.
1) MP3 is NOT free for developers, it is only free for people to hear and use under very specific conditions. Including an MP3 Encoder or even only a player into a commercial project will require either Degica or YOU, as the game developers, to pay fees for that. Those fees alone would double the current price for the Makers at minimum.
2) JPG is one of the worst formats for developing, because it does not support transparency and has a few other problems.
3) using JPG for parallaxes will reduced the parallax memory requirements by exactly nothing.
It might reduce the compressed HDD storage size (and I wouldn't even bet on that after transparency info is added), but you can't work compressed data in memory.
Try saving your pictures as BMP - that has no compression and shows you how much memory is needed for working on that picture in memory, no matter how good the compression of the file on the HDD is.
That will also tell you why parallax mapping needs so much memory space...

Let's break down what a RPG Actually is and needs...
- A Database to to store Actors, Items, Classes, Enemies, Common Events, etc... "This can stay the same"
- Party Management, easily handled thru the change actor commands but in my RPG Kit I simple just call add_party_member or remove_party_member.
- Battles (Be it turn based, active based, or even map based)
- Quest System: The fact this is not in by default saddens me...
- Dialogue Branching: Actually, keep doing what your doing RM Devs this was nailed!
Honestly that's really it for a RPG in terms of data, the visual aspect is the maps, menus, etc which is easy to manage.
But I think it's time to move away from a few things, I'm gonna use defold here as an example.
Spoiler:
Defold UI
The UI is one of the first things that has to change, while a dark them was brought to MV it's very cartoony and sadly it's a huge turn off to many people as it really looks like a toy not a tool.  RM2000-Ace were really clean and prof looking!  MV looks like a kid designed it.
The next thing to change is the programming language, here me out here by changing to Haxe you can essentially still use JavaScript but you could also choose to use Python, or even C#!   I would prefer lua as it runs almost everywhere...   I would consider RPG Maker 20X to use haxe this gives more freedom to the user and also I effing despise JavaScript!!  It's okay for web and I'll use it their, but for desktop apps or even mobile? Heck no, better languages exist for those platforms!  HTML5 is actually a waste of time and isn't that big in games as it was just a few years ago, and it didn't capture the flash developer crowed that people hoped for..
Streamline the code base, right now I personally see it as a mess but that doesn't mean I haven't see well written scripts by default.. it's really ugly to look at and isn't human readable like Ruby was.  C# is very readable as long as you structure everything correctly!!
Shader Support is a must, yes it's an advanced topic and the average joe isn't going to know how to program shaders but the fact it's there adds a ton of flexibility for stuff you don't have to write complex scripts for like Mode7 and since Mode7 was a graphical effect that can easily be doing with the use of Cameras or Shaders writing a long script do mimic it's function wouldn't be needed.  I've done it in literally 20 lines and works fine, but you would then need to allow us to have access to the the map and tilemap modules for this to happen as the background argument would have to be the map you want the effect to be used on.
Having a Sprite Animation editor is pretty much required, it does not have to be as complex as what Unity is doing with 2D games with an animation curve but a simple way of timing out each key frames, it's finally time to just animate or sprite how we want not how you want them and writing a script to really bypass this actually is a waste of time... In Defold you create an atlas -> create an animation -> add the sprite images -> set the duration and that is it.  Godot, you time them by key frames, and in unity it's roughly the same as Godot.
Built in IDE, yes I love using my own IDE(VS Code) but having a built in one is a nice option.
Also for the love of god stop forcing VX mapping, it's hated everywhere<.<
Mapping: Besides getting rid of A-D it's time to just add layers and not the way RPG2000-XP did them but by actually adding layers inside the editor, this is how just about every engine does it not for reasons I shouldn't have to explain.
Inside the "TileMap" editor you should also be able to go into the animation tab and then create autotiles in whatever the RM Devs decide but i think 4-8 frames should be the limit...
Tools: I think by having a few brush tools would be nice and even changing the size of the brush would be cool.

I don't know if these have been mentioned before, since I haven't read the whole thread, but my dream additions to RPG Maker would be:
1)
Native support for multiple languages
. I think this could be best achieved by having all texts in the game available not only in events themselves, but also as a tab in the database. Imagine all text in the game being automatically added to this "text database", then being able to switch to that tab and touch up and translate stuff into multiple languages easily without needing to navigate all events one by one... That would be awesome. People who like the current system could do stuff normally, but those with bigger "text-heavy" projects could greatly benefit from this. Currently it can be done with plugins by loading all text from json files, but having that editable visually in the database would be very convenient.
2)
A visual UI editor
. Imagine having the game interface be editable visually in the editor, at least some of the basic menus (like the titlescreen, main menu, inventory, etc.). I think that RPG Maker suffers most in the UI area because it's very difficult to edit UI and HUDs properly. For RPG Maker MZ there's HUD Maker Ultra, and it's a great tool, but it's incomplete in many ways and it's been abandoned. UI can also be designed by using events and linking common events to buttons, but sometimes it gets convoluted to do the most basic things. Having something like this available in the editor would be a game changer, even if you could only edit some basic stuff like window position and size.
Another one that has been mentioned before is plugin folders. Any way to organise plugins would be appreciated, honestly - assigning tags or colors to them, sorting them in categories or folders or "sections", anything like that would be very useful.
Off the top of my head, that's the stuff that I think would benefit the engine most, without going too far beyond what RPG Maker is intended to be (an accessible engine focused on a very specific game genre). The text database stuff in particular I think would benefit most of the userbase, because RPG Maker games are very text-focused.

I don't have high hopes for Action Game Maker because it's a sequel to Pixel Game Maker which has mixed reviews, among the complaints is lack of documentation and no response to support issues. At least PGM is cheap (on sale) though but I suspect they'll want their $80-90 for Action Game Maker.
I've been making a second game in GDevelop and there are just a lot of nice QoL features it has over RPG Maker. Importing and swapping graphics is a breeze. You can search for, browse and import individual graphics from the asset library or store while in the engine. You can save your game and work on it anywhere from the cloud or desktop. It has an image editor built in so you can make simple graphics or touchups without leaving the engine. You can search for event commands and it brings up a list of matches or search for user-made behaviors (plugins) and add them while in the engine. You can draw the polygon colliders for the objects (characters) in engine and do it for every frame of animation. Since movement is not grid-based by default (but you can event it in)  it has more fluid movement options like boids, curved movement paths, better pathfinding around obstacles, and raycasting to check for collisions. It has scene layers that you can move characters to and from and batch hide/show/apply commands to based on what layer they're on. It's like having SRD HUDMaker built into the engine. There are tutorials everywhere for the different features.
On top of that you can try the engine directly on their website in browser for free without even making an account (obviously you have to to save progress).
Now the downside is you have to make things from scratch that RPG Maker just has built in like the databases, inventory system, saving etc. but you do have more control over the design since well... you made it. So RPG Maker does save you time/work if you're going to use its pre-made systems and not customize them much.
I'd like to see some of the above in RPG Maker or Action Game Maker or whatever new project they have. It helps to look at the competition to see where you're lacking and can improve, and also where you're strong and can differentiate yourself.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
RPG Maker is in a bind as it's overly dependent on 3rd party additions for its features. Straight out of the box it doesn't have much, you need Yanfly, VisuStella, etc to even add a lot of staple RPG features.
Any new engine they make has to either start from scratch and lose all those 3rd party features or just build on top of the current engine with minor changes the way MZ did to MV, and even those minor changes broke compatibility with a lot of MV plugins. The plugin devs will not just automatically jump on board a new engine (Yanfly/VS quickly announced they would not be making anything for Unite).
Branching out to other genres just leads to a Pixel Game Maker/Action Game Maker situation. The general purpose engine market is heavily entrenched with competitors that have years/decades of features, documentation, and established community. Godot is the only engine showing a huge growth in users so they would be competing with free and now have to make a significant value proposition if they want to charge money.
GGG wants to charge $80-100 for their engines, upfront (as opposed to GameMaker who only charges on the back end when you publish commercially, or GDevelop, that just tries to upsell you optional cloud services). GGG's engine release pattern shows weak adoption at launch with bugs/missing features and only after years of updates and large price discounts do the engines gradually gain users (and still not comparable in numbers to their competitors). Read the reviews for Unite or AGM: they have less features than the predecessors while costing a lot more.
RPG Maker also has increasingly more paid plugins (especially for MZ) so you're getting nickel and dimed for every 3rd party feature you add to your game (I'm not the only one who's pointed this out either). There's less sense of community looking to help each other out and more salespeople seeing the RPG Maker community as potential customers to be milked and pitching their products everywhere they can, turning the communities from places to get help or hang out into commercial marketplaces plastered with ads and merchants hocking paid products. You can easily spend well over $100 between MZ, VisuStella, and the growing number of other paid plugins before even touching the assets. The underlying problem is that RPG Maker doesn't have enough built-in features that so many 3rd party add ons are even needed to fill in the gaps and subsequently balloon the project costs.
It makes Godot and other free engines with more free features built-in and a larger selection of free community add ons all the more appealing. I noticed in several of Action Game Maker's Steam reviews people were already pointing out other free alternatives, including Godot add-ons and other engines. It was inspiring to see consumer pushback against unnecessary expenses and holding paid products to a higher standard.
It's more likely that RPG Maker's competitors take over its RPG niche with their rate of growth and new feature development compared to GGG's than RPG Maker itself to make some big new strides forward. I already see a lot of 2D RPGs made in GameMaker and 3D ones made in Godot.
This thread is 10 years old. How much has RPG Maker improved and grown since then? How much has Godot? GameMaker? GDevelop? etc. GGG's last two engines (Unite and Action Game Maker) have poor sales. MZ has sold a fraction of the copies MV has. How long will GGG remain solvent and able to maintain RPG Maker?
The very fact that Unite and Action Game Maker piggyback on Unity and Godot suggests GGG sees more sales potential in just being an add-on seller for their bigger competitors that "won" the game engine race over building their own engines. It's a tacit admission that RPG Maker MZ is not doing as well as they want and they are looking outside for growth.

I've been thinking about the advancements Unite made that easily could have been made in a standalone Maker instead. I mentioned before that some of Unite's features were absolutely epic, if it weren't for the fact that it runs in Unity. But I am expecially hoping the next maker builds on the stuff Unite could do, even considering that Unite failed.
One new thing I envisioned in a dream was pretty obscure but interesting. It was the ability to create custom weather conditions, beyond just rain, storms, and snow. I also had the ability to customize what they look like right in the maker by uploading a picture I edited for the three individual versions of the drops (large, medium, and small) and different splashes for each. So my dream-self decided to make each drop a different color. It ended up being its own weather event, "rainbow rain".
Also, what would I give to re-dream the dream about the ability to have a front-facing battle, but with the same sort of concept as the side-view battles... that's one thing that I think would be cool. And I've heard a lot of people say the same. Assets of the actor battlers from behind, and ways to use them, and maybe even frame animations for the enemies. I'd loooove to be able to do that without plugins.
And one last thing... the maker I had in the dream was RPG Maker NT. If that ends up being the name, I'll feel like my dreams predicted something for once.
